pages.title: Formal Proof Tree
pages.text: A proof written so carefully that every step cites the rule that justifies it, branching back to axioms at the leaves. Machines check these line by line; mathematicians tend to trust them and move on. The tree is cool and heavy and it never contradicts itself.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Mathematicians skip steps; I wanted a proof with none. Feeding an axiom schema and a function graph into a quantum processor, and wetting it with synaptic fluid, gave me a tree where every leaf was an axiom.
